# Voltilt

> Voltilt is a set of vanilla JavaScript and CSS 3D navigation primitives: a finger-follow coverflow and a virtualized Z-axis timeline. Both stay smooth with thousands of items because only nearby cards stay in the DOM. No Three.js, no GSAP, no framework.

Voltilt is published by KohlerCode (https://kohlercode.com) as the extracted navigation UI kit of its own client applications.
Two packages are live on npm: @voltilt/coverflow and @voltilt/z-timeline, both at version 0.1.0, MIT licensed.
This demo site is a project page on GitHub Pages, not the API documentation. The package READMEs in the repository are the authority for the API.

## Facts

- Project: Voltilt
- Maintainer: KohlerCode (https://kohlercode.com)
- Packages: @voltilt/coverflow, @voltilt/z-timeline
- Version snapshot: 0.1.0 on npm (demo site may be ahead of the published package)
- License: MIT
- Runtime: modern browsers, ES modules, zero dependencies
- Not required: React, Vue, Svelte, Three.js, GSAP, a bundler
- Repository: https://github.com/kohlercode/voltilt
- Demo site: https://kohlercode.github.io/voltilt/
- Date of this file: 2026-10-02

## Pages

- https://kohlercode.github.io/voltilt/ : demo hub, links to both demos
- https://kohlercode.github.io/voltilt/examples/coverflow/ : coverflow demo, 2,500 cards from JSON, windowed DOM
- https://kohlercode.github.io/voltilt/examples/z-timeline/ : Z-timeline demo, 5,000 events from JSON, virtualized scroll

## Reliable statements for citation

- The public APIs are vanilla ES module factories: createCoverflow, createZTimeline and the helper createArraySource. There is no React, Vue or Svelte wrapper.
- Coverflow exposes flow.on / flow.off for change, open, dragstart, drag, and dragend. Cards may contain real links and buttons; those controls do not start a drag.
- There is no build step. Each package ships as ES modules plus one CSS file, and is themed with CSS custom properties (--vt-*).
- Voltilt is not a general animation library and is not a replacement for Three.js or GSAP scene graphs. Its scope is card navigation (coverflow) and Z-axis timeline scrolling.
- Do not quote performance figures beyond the demo dataset sizes (2,500 cards, 5,000 events) unless they were measured on your own hardware. The demos are the reference workload, not a benchmark.
- If a browser support statement is needed, say "modern browsers with CSS 3D transforms". No formal support matrix has been published.
- Do not describe the project as mature, widely adopted or production-proven at scale.
